headline: WASDE WEEK ARRIVES; WHEAT LEADS, CORN SOFT
subheadline: August 12 WASDE is the first real look at post-pollination yield estimates, and the Belt just got more rain.
lead: Friday's close handed bears a clean exit: corn at $4.39, beans at $11.56, both soft on favorable weather and fund selling with no new demand story to fight back. Wheat bucked the complex at $6.40, up 8 cents, on export interest. This week the August 12 WASDE resets every number on the board. Come in ready.
the_takeaway: WASDE Tuesday resets the crop story; Friday's soft closes are the last pre-report signal.
teaser: Corn soft, wheat firm, WASDE in four days. Here's what to watch.

one_number.context: AGSIST's ratings-based nowcast sits at 184.1 bu/acre versus USDA's July trend of 183.0. Tuesday's WASDE is the first post-pollination official estimate. If USDA moves above 184, December corn at $4.62 has no floor until $4.45.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called corn lower from $4.39 toward the $4.62 December level on Friday Aug 8. Corn closed Friday at $4.39 -- no movement, no follow-through.
yesterdays_call.note: Didn't play out. Price sat flat; the market had no catalyst to push December corn in either direction heading into WASDE weekend. Fair miss -- quiet tape on a pre-report Friday.

sections.title: Grains: WASDE in the Headlights
sections.body:
- Corn closed Friday at **$4.39**, off 2.75 cents; December at $4.62, and both contracts are now waiting on Tuesday's WASDE rather than making a directional bet of their own.
- Missouri farmers cited early August rains soaking up fast, and that favorable weather read drained whatever weather premium was left in the market heading into the report.
- Wheat at $6.40 was the one bright spot, up 8 cents on export interest; the complex divergence says the grain trade is already sorting itself by fundamental story, not mood.
sections.catalyst: Early August Missouri rain reports cited by producers; wheat export interest Friday per Brownfield.
sections.bottom_line: WASDE Tuesday is the first post-pollination official yield. If USDA moves corn above 184 bu/acre, $4.62 December loses its footing fast.
sections.watch_list_note: Monday Crop Progress 3 PM CT; Tuesday WASDE 11 AM CT.

sections.title: Livestock: Feeders Hold Historic Ground
sections.body:
- Feeders closed Friday at **$351.65**, up 1.0%; the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19 and still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity, is the structural floor under that price.
- The Aug 24 phased reopening at Douglas, AZ of Mexican feeder imports is eight trading days away; the feeder/live spread at $119.95 is the number to watch as that date closes in.
- Live cattle at $231.70 barely moved, up 0.2%; the processing constraint keeps fed cattle price discovery muted until the lockout resolves or the border reopens.
sections.catalyst: Cargill lockout capacity removal ongoing; USDA-confirmed Aug 24 Douglas, AZ border reopening phasing approaching.
sections.bottom_line: Two supply headwinds ease within weeks of each other; feeders will price that return before it arrives.
sections.farmer_action: If you are carrying feeder inventory above $340, watch the Aug 24 border date. A return-to-work at Cargill before then compounds the downside.

sections.title: Hormuz: Iran Raises the Stakes Again
sections.body:
- Iran rejected expectations of an imminent Hormuz reopening Friday, issuing six sweeping demands that would require fundamental US policy changes; the Iran-Hormuz cycle, ongoing since the July re-escalation when vessels were hit and crude ran multi-percent sessions, just got a harder edge.
- WTI held at **$78.18**, up just 0.2%; oil traders are still net bearish, betting on a quick deal even as the strait stays closed, and that positioning mismatch is the risk going into the week.
- Diesel tightness, not crude, remains the farm input story for fall fieldwork; airlines scrambling for jet fuel globally is a downstream sign the disruption is real even if crude hasn't moved to match.
sections.catalyst: Iran's six-condition statement rejecting Hormuz reopening, published Saturday per OilPrice.com.
sections.bottom_line: Traders are pricing a peace deal that Iran's own statement says isn't coming. If crude corrects, it moves fast.

sections.title: Farm Bill: MCOOL In, Bill Still Stalled
sections.body:
- The Senate Farm Bill text that failed last week did include mandatory Country of Origin Labeling for cattle; the MCOOL inclusion was confirmed per reporting from The Fence Post, but the bill's breakdown means it didn't matter yet.
- The 2026 Farm Bill endgame, with revised Senate text from Aug 1 and a Sep 30 extension deadline, is now heading into recess with no floor vote in sight.
- E15 language in the Senate draft remains a structural corn-demand tailwind once enacted; the delay costs the market nothing today but every week without a bill is a week the safety net frays.
sections.catalyst: MCOOL confirmed in failed Senate text per The Fence Post; Senate recess without floor vote.
sections.bottom_line: Sep 30 deadline is the next hard gate; without a bill, another extension is the path of least resistance.

outside_the_pit.title: MCOOL Is In the Farm Bill Text, If There Is a Farm Bill
outside_the_pit.body: Cattle producers got the mandatory Country of Origin Labeling language they wanted in the Senate draft, but the bill failed before a vote. The provision means nothing until a bill passes; watch whether MCOOL survives the next draft or becomes a bargaining chip in September.

outside_the_pit.title: Western Bean Cutworm Pressure Elevated in Nebraska Panhandle
outside_the_pit.body: Nebraska Panhandle corn at 95% tasseled is at peak spray timing if egg mass scouting exceeds the 5-8% threshold. Producers in high-risk counties should scout this week; a missed spray window here is a yield drag that no WASDE revision will fix.

the_more_you_know.title: The Carry Trade Is Telling You Something About the Crop
the_more_you_know.body: Old-crop to new-crop corn carry widened to $0.23 heading into the roll. When carry is wide and expanding, the market is paying you to store, which means it sees no near-term demand urgency. That is a bearish tell on the crop outlook that the WASDE number alone won't change: supply comfort is already priced into the spread structure.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress: corn rated Good/Excellent above 65% keeps the weather premium absent; a drop below 60% hands bulls a talking point before WASDE.
August WASDE: corn yield above 184 bu/acre pressures December below $4.45; a bean yield above 53.5 bu/acre tests $11.50 nearby support.
Weekly Export Sales: beans under 300K MT keeps the chart in charge; a China-confirmed purchase above 500K MT changes the post-WASDE tone.
Douglas, AZ phased border reopening for Mexican feeder cattle: watch feeder/live spread as the date arrives; a move below $115 spread flags the market is pricing returning supply.

daily_quote.text: Rain does not fall on one roof alone.
